newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Airlines pilots to vote on wage cut plan.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Airlines pilots to vote on wage cut plan.

text.p: Canadian Airlines International pilots plan to vote this week on whether to accept a 10 percent wage cut to try to save the airline.
The pilot vote is scheduled in spite of a refusal by other union leaders to put the proposed salary cut to a member vote.
"Invariably it's the pilots who go first and we're offering that again," Canadian Airline Pilots Association member Michael Lynch said in a report by the Canadian Press.
The airline lost C$1 billion in recent years with its president Kevin Benson calling for the 10-percent pay cut last week as part of a "do-or-die" rescue package.
Ballots were to be mailed Monday or Tuesday to about 1,150 pilots and the results will be added up before the Nov 30 deadline Canadian gave its six unions to accept the cut.
The pilots, who earn between C$35,000 and C$200,000 a year, make up 10 percent of Canadian's payroll, Lynch said.
Calgary-based Canadian Airlines has 16,400 employees, including those in its Canadian Regional Airlines Ltd unit. Union employees make up about 12,000 of the total.
Of its six unions, the International Association of Machinists & Aerospace Workers and the Canadian Auto Workers make up about 9,000 of the airline's unionized workforce.
CAW president Buzz Hargrove opposed a free employee vote on the wage cut and said he does not believe the airline will shut down if a deal is not reached. He called the crisis "a charade."

Canadian's turnaround plan includes wage cuts, reducing the number of routes in Canada and getting a C$48 million cut in annual fees to American Airlines, which owns 33 per cent of Canadian and has a 25 percent voting interest in the airline.
CAI has a fleet of 80 jets, not including those in its Canadian Regional unit.
